articles.title: 比亚迪腾势汽车李慧：易三方 Evo 是全球独一无二的硬核技术平台，友商追赶了易三方超过三年也没追上
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，博主 @向北不断电 今日发文，称腾势 N8 的优势依然明显，也是市面上为数不多闭眼买的车型，并提到易三方 Evo 独一档强大。腾势汽车总经理李慧随后转发，并表示易三方 Evo 是全球独一无二的硬核技术平台，目前任何一个汽车品牌都没有，友商追赶了易三方超过三年也没有追赶上。易三方 Evo 让腾势 N8 更安全、更灵活、更澎湃、更高效！据IT之家此前报道，腾势 N8 于 11 月 12 日正式上市，共推出 6 款配置车型，提供后置单电机两驱与易三方三电机四驱两种动力形式，官方指导价区间为 26.99 万-32.99 万元。延伸阅读易三方（e³）是比亚迪旗下腾势品牌独有的整车智能控制技术平台，于 2024 年 9 月随腾势 Z9GT 首次量产搭载。该平台由三电机独立驱动技术、后轮双电机独立转向技术、VMC 整车运动控制技术、CTB 电池车身一体化技术四大核心技术组成，可实现后轮双向最大 20° 的独立转向，并衍生出极致转向、圆规掉头、易三方泊车、低附路面增稳系统、智能蟹行等功能。此次腾势 N8 全球首搭的「易三方 Evo」是该平台的升级版本。据官方介绍，其在效率上有所提升，可使整车续航提升超过 60km，并进一步强化安全能力，通过了高速直线侧后追尾稳行、湿滑路面高速连续避障、夜间及弯道湿滑路面侧后追尾稳行等四大工况测试，同时全系标配第二代刀片电池与 CTB 电池车身一体化技术。腾势 N8 定位「科技新境宽五座 SUV」，于 2026 年 11 月 12 日上市，提供纯电与插混两种动力。该车车身尺寸为 5150×1999×1820mm，轴距 3075mm，最小转弯半径 4.5m，后轮转向角度为 ±10°，0-100km/h 加速时间为 4.3 秒。

articles.title: 三星电子非半导体板块内存平均采购价今年前九个月同比暴涨 263%
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，据韩联社当地时间 18 日报道，根据三星电子同日发布的详细三季报，该企业负责非半导体板块的 DX（设备体验）部门今年 1~9 月的内存平均采购价格同比暴涨 263%。而在相同时间内，DX 部门的移动应用处理器平均采购价格上涨了 8%，旗下 MX（移动体验）业务的 Galaxy 智能手机平均销售价格仅上涨了 13%。另一组数据显示，DX 部门 1~9 月原材料采购额达 62.4307 万亿韩元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 3,132.77 亿元人民币），同比增长 8.9%；移动设备内存采购总额达 7.6993 万亿韩元（现汇率约合 386.35 亿元人民币），占整体的 12.3%。内存成本暴涨但终端设备售价涨幅有限，导致 MX 与 NW（网络）业务整体连续第二个季度出现亏损。MX 业务在 Q3 财报电话会议中表示，计划以差异化的旗舰产品为核心，以硬件和形态创新增强用户吸引力，并通过灵活市场响应和运营改进降低利润下滑影响。

articles.title: 我国成功发射卫星互联网低轨 30 组卫星
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，今天（20 日）19 时 59 分，我国在海南商业航天发射场使用长征八号甲运载火箭，成功将卫星互联网低轨 30 组卫星发射升空，卫星顺利进入预定轨道，发射任务获得圆满成功。据IT之家了解，11 月 9 日 4 时 24 分，长征十二号运载火箭在海南商业航天发射场点火起飞，随后成功将卫星互联网低轨 29 组卫星送入预定轨道。延伸阅读卫星互联网低轨卫星组网属于中国星网 GW 星座，这是我国首个巨型卫星互联网计划，也是我国首个空天一体化 6G 卫星互联网计划。整个星座规划部署 12992 颗卫星，分为 GW-A59 与 GW-A2 两个子星座：前者计划部署 6080 颗，主要分布在 500 公里以下轨道；后者计划部署 6912 颗，轨道高度约 1145 公里，轨道倾角覆盖 30 度至 85 度。按照相关规划，GW 星座将在 2029 年年底前完成约 1300 颗卫星部署，并计划于 2035 年完成全部 12992 颗卫星组网。2026 年 10 月 9 日，国产卫星系统在中国第 16 次北冰洋考察期间完成首次极区试验，实现跨越南北极的视频通话，测试使用的正是中国星网 GW 星座，最高上下行速率约 30Mbps。而本次使用的长征八号甲运载火箭由航天科技集团一院研制，是长征八号运载火箭的改进型号，采用 3.35 米直径氢氧末级和 5.2 米直径整流罩，全箭高超 50 米，起飞质量约 371 吨，起飞推力约 480 吨，700 公里太阳同步轨道运载能力提升至 7 吨级，专为高密度、快速组网发射而设计。

articles.title: 加州禁令引发连锁反应，Waymo 暂停全美 Robotaxi 高速公路服务
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，当地时间 18 日，据英国《卫报》报道，Alphabet 旗下的 Waymo 在美国全面暂停了无人驾驶出租车的高速公路服务，恢复时间未定。此前，加州因 Waymo 车辆近期发生的交通事件，禁止其在州内高速公路行驶，Waymo 随后将暂停范围扩大至全美。Waymo 此前在旧金山湾区、洛杉矶、凤凰城、迈阿密和奥斯汀提供高速公路无人驾驶出租车服务，并在拉斯维加斯、达拉斯和丹佛等多个地区运营城市道路乘车服务，面向城区的服务此次不受影响。Waymo 发言人通过电子邮件回应称，公司暂时停止了所有运营市场的商业无人驾驶高速公路服务，但仍会让经过培训的自动驾驶专员坐在驾驶位，继续开展高速公路测试。暂停措施从 11 月 11 日开始实施，发言人没有透露恢复时间。同一天，加州机动车管理局也禁止 Waymo 无人驾驶出租车在州内高速公路行驶。该局发言人乔纳森 · 格罗夫曼指出，禁令与两起交通事件有关，其中一起是 3 辆 Waymo 无人驾驶车辆闯入施工区域。其中，施工区域事件发生在 11 月 5 日，另一起事件发生在 6 日，涉及加州公路巡警车辆，地点位于旧金山的一条高速公路。11 月 6 日事件的视频上周在社交媒体上广泛传播。画面显示，一辆 Waymo 试图绕过正在实施临时交通管制的加州公路巡警车辆。格罗夫曼指出，Waymo 车辆多次闯入仍在施工的区域，现场有施工人员、车辆和设备。加州机动车管理局因此认定，Waymo 的无人驾驶高速公路运营对公共安全构成直接威胁。而在 5 月 18 日，就已经发生了类似事件。Waymo 发言人则称，近期车辆在加州 101 号公路施工区域发生的事件没有造成人员受伤或车辆碰撞。格罗夫曼指出，加州禁令不仅禁止 Waymo 在高速公路运营无人驾驶车辆，也禁止开展无人驾驶测试。只有 Waymo 向监管部门证明采取了有效整改措施，解决引发禁令的问题后，限制措施才会解除。相关阅读：《美国加州叫停 Waymo 高速公路运营：无人驾驶出租车曾试图超越公路巡警》

articles.title: 《堡垒之夜》致敬《GTA 4》，重现主角 Niko 表哥 Roman“名台词”
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，据 IGN 今天（20 日）晚间报道，《堡垒之夜》新增了一系列致敬《GTA 4》的隐藏任务，连游戏中的主要角色 Roman Bellic 那句经典的“表弟！咱们出去玩吧！”也被做成了彩蛋。11 月 19 日《GTA 6》正式发售当天，Epic Games 在《堡垒之夜》中开放了 6 项隐藏任务。玩家需要完成香蕉人皮利布置的任务，全部完成后可获得总计 12 万经验值。这些任务都在致敬《GTA 4》中 Roman 频繁打电话骚扰表弟、游戏主角 Niko 的经典桥段。玩家会在《堡垒之夜》中接到 Peely 的电话，随后按照要求完成附近的任务。其中一项任务要求玩家击倒保龄球瓶，呼应 Roman 经常打电话约 Niko 打保龄球的情节。任务说明更是直接写着：“表弟！咱们出去玩吧！”其他任务则围绕《堡垒之夜》现有地图上的彩蛋展开，包括探索隐藏的藏宝洞穴、破解类似《塞尔达传说》的雕像谜题，以及参加一场有趣的橡皮鸭竞赛。面对本周发售的《GTA 6》，《堡垒之夜》的表现依然相当稳健，常驻大逃杀模式的玩家数量仍达到数百万。据IT之家了解，Epic Games 还通过当前赛季的奖励活动吸引玩家，提供解锁为期两周免费使用游戏道具商店权限的机会，大批玩家正努力完成任务以获取这项福利。《GTA 6》方面，R 星尚未公布具体销量。不过，据估计，游戏发售前的预购量就达到 2000 万份，取得巨大成功自是不言而喻。

articles.title: Take-Two 前 CEO 费德：《GTA 6》将是 AI 时代前夜最后的“传统”3A 大作
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，Take-Two 前 CEO 本 · 费德认为，《GTA 6》将成为 AI 时代全面到来前最后一部采用传统开发模式打造的 3A 大作，游戏行业也将由此告别一个时代。费德在《财富》杂志撰文称：“《GTA 6》的发布将成为一场文化盛事，带来史诗般的游戏体验。我相信它会是一部杰作，但也会是同类作品中的最后一部。”IT之家获悉，他认为，原因并非 R 星的质量把控能力下降，也不是 AI 能让游戏开发更快、更省钱，而是《GTA 6》代表着一种即将被 AI 颠覆的创作模式的巅峰。费德指出，游戏开发过程中，改变方向甚至放弃原有创意，都可能耗费大量时间和技术资源，AI 可以大幅降低改变主意的成本。费德将 AI 对游戏行业的影响，比作摄影术对绘画的冲击：“摄影术问世时，许多视觉艺术家担心生计受到威胁，其中一些人的担忧确实成真了：委托画家绘制肖像的市场崩溃了。但也有人开始思考另一个问题：接下来我们还能创作什么？摆脱了忠实还原现实的要求后，他们开创了全新甚至颠覆性的艺术形式，包括印象派、立体主义和抽象艺术。我猜想，未来的文化史学家看待《GTA 6》，就像艺术史学家看待最后一批伟大的写实主义画家一样。”在他看来，《GTA 6》是一种创作模式在媒介边界被打破、全新艺术形式涌现之前所达到的最高成就。

articles.title: 39.5 亿年！河北发现亚洲已知最古老岩石
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，自然资源部中国地质调查局今日宣布，近日，中国地质科学院地质研究所万渝生研究员团队在《自然》期刊发表研究成果。该团队在河北冀东地区发现距今 39.5 亿年的古老岩石，这是目前我国乃至亚洲已知最古老的岩石，也是全球第二古老的岩石。研究表明，地球在 39.5 亿年前可能已出现某种形式的俯冲构造活动，为冥古宙时期地幔已经发生亏损提供了直接证据。地球诞生于约 45 亿年前，但最早几亿年的地质记录极难保存，能够追溯到地球童年时期的样本十分稀缺。此次发现的岩石为奥长花岗质片麻岩，产自冀东地区新建立的石门杂岩中。研究人员利用锆石铀 — 铅定年方法测定其形成年龄为 39.5 亿年。此前全球公认最古老的岩石是加拿大 Acasta 片麻岩，年龄约为 40 亿年。IT之家获悉，这次发现，把我国最古老岩石的记录往前推进了 1.5 亿年，和世界最古老岩石的年龄差距，也缩小到 5000 万年。该发现回答了两个长期悬而未决的问题。一是确定某种形式俯冲构造机制的形成时间。岩石样品化学分析显示，其原始物质曾接触过地表水，随后被带入地下约 50 公里深处，在高压、较低温度条件下发生部分熔融。这意味着，早在 39.5 亿年前，地球内部就已经出现了将地表物质送进深部的构造力量，而非此前一些观点认为的直到更晚时期才启动。二是确定地幔和地壳分家的时间。学界关于这一问题长期存在争议，关键原因在于地幔亏损的信息很少留存在锆石的铪同位素中。此次发现表明，地幔早在 43 亿年前就已经发生了明显亏损 —— 通俗地说，地球内部很早就开始“分家”，较轻的物质上浮形成地壳，较重的物质留在地幔，这一过程的启动时间比以往许多研究认为的更早。

articles.title: 近 400 马力的纯电小钢炮：大众发布 ID. Polo GTI Clubsport 概念车
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，2026 年是大众 GTI 诞生 50 周年。为了庆祝这一里程碑，大众不仅推出了 ID. Polo GTI 和 ID.3 Neo GTI 两款新车，还打破了本田思域 Type R 保持的纽博格林赛道前驱车圈速纪录，进一步证明 GTI 的性能实力。周年庆祝活动还没结束，大众又带来了首款纯电 GTI Clubsport。新车名为 ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept，将于本月在德国埃森车展首次亮相，最引人注目的变化是动力大幅提升。新车与量产版 ID. Polo GTI 同样基于 MEB+ 平台打造，采用单电机前驱布局，换装了尺寸更大的 APP550 电机，与后驱的 ID.7、ID.3 Neo GTI 等车型采用相同的电机。相比普通版 GTI 的 226 马力（166kW），Clubsport 的最大功率提高至 367 马力（270kW），增幅达到 63%。大众还通过电池控制系统，让动力系统能够在短时间内输出 394 马力（290kW），峰值扭矩也从 290N·m 跃升至 550N·m。据IT之家了解，大众对车辆进行了大量重新设计，为此开发了全新副车架，以确保前轮能够承受更大的动力。最终，Clubsport 的 0-100km/h加速时间缩短至 4.7 秒，最高时速达到 240km/h。相比量产版 ID. Polo GTI，Clubsport 则更加激进，不仅增加了发动机盖通风口和尾门顶部的大型扰流板，还采用了夸张的宽体轮拱，造型足以媲美世界拉力锦标赛赛车。Clubsport 的外观俨然是一辆赛道利器，内饰同样充满赛车氛围。RECARO 桶形赛车座椅、五点式安全带，以及喷涂经典 Tornado 红色的后部防滚架一应俱全，仪表台和其他多处饰板也用上了 ArtVelours 超细绒面材质。

articles.title: 零跑与欧宝正式签署合作协议：共同开发全新 C 级 SUV 车型，预计 2028 年开售
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，零跑科技创始人、董事长兼 CEO 朱江明与欧宝 CEO Florian Huettl 正式签署合作协议，双方将共同开发一款全新的 C 级 SUV 车型。目前，双方项目团队已分别在中国杭州和德国吕塞尔斯海姆的联合项目中心开展相关工作，本次签约将进一步推动该项目的开发进程。官方表示，全新欧宝 C 级 SUV 车型的开发是零跑与 Stellantis 集团合作关系的重要组成部分，也是 Stellantis 集团近期发布的 FaSTLane 2030 战略增长计划中的一项重要举措。IT之家获悉，新车预计将于 2028 年正式开启销售，计划于西班牙萨拉戈萨工厂生产。新车将采用零跑汽车的核心零部件，并融合欧宝标志性的设计语言、座舱人体工程学、底盘工程以及高级照明系统和座椅技术。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，独立开发团队 Magic Pie 宣布旗下开放世界生存游戏《POLYARIS》将于 2027 年 1 月 20 日登陆 Steam 平台，IT之家附游戏商品页（https://store.steampowered.com/app/2979810/POLYARIS/?snr=1_5_1100__1100&utm_source=steamwidget）。据介绍，《POLYARIS》是一款融合滑雪、制作与生存玩法的开放世界游戏。故事发生在一场核弹袭击后的世界，主角乘坐的飞机意外坠毁，被困在挪威与俄罗斯边境的极寒地带，却也因此侥幸躲过了核爆的直接冲击。由于与外界彻底失去联系，周边居民也离奇失踪，玩家必须在这片冰天雪地中设法生存，同时调查神秘核爆事件及居民失踪背后的真相，寻找逃离这片荒无人烟的北极圈的方法。在严酷的极地环境中，玩家需要利用滑雪板和小船穿越广阔的雪原与冰海，搜寻生存物资，还可以通过钓鱼获取食物，并收集各种材料，制作维持生存所需的装备。除了随时可能危及生命的严寒天气和猛烈暴风雪，北极熊、野狼等凶猛掠食者也会在野外伺机袭击玩家。此外，心怀恶意的敌对掠夺者同样构成威胁，玩家必须时刻保持警惕，才能在这片被遗弃的极地世界中活下去。游戏图赏：

articles.title: Linux KVM Flaw CVE-2026-99312 Lets Guest VMs Access Host Memory on AMD Hosts
articles.content: A flaw in KVM, the hypervisor built into the Linux kernel, let researchers read about 127 GB of a cloud server's memory from inside a virtual machine of their own on DigitalOcean. On a shared server, that memory can include other customers' virtual machines. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-99312, affects only hosts with AMD processors and nested virtualization enabled. Fixed kernels shipped

articles.title: 长城汽车旗下坦克品牌第 100 万台量产车下线
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，坦克品牌今日宣布，第 1,000,000 台量产车下线。据IT之家此前报道，11 月 1 日，坦克品牌全球销量 100 万辆。公开信息显示，2020 年 7 月，长城汽车在成都车展上正式发布了“坦克 · WEY”平台，并亮相了该平台首款车型 ——WEY 坦克 300。2020 年 12 月，坦克 300 作为长城汽车旗下 WEY（魏牌）体系内的车型正式上市。2021 年 4 月，坦克品牌在上海车展上正式宣布独立运营，成为长城汽车继哈弗、WEY（魏牌）、长城皮卡、欧拉之后的第五大整车品牌。延伸阅读坦克品牌 Logo 由字母 T 和 U 组成，其中 T 代表坦克品牌、科技和潮流的定位，U 则代表用户和共创。目前，坦克品牌已形成包括坦克 300、坦克 400、坦克 500、坦克 700 等在内的产品序列，并引入了 Hi4-T 和 Hi4-Z 两大混动架构。根据长城汽车 2025 年年报，坦克品牌 2025 年全年累计销量为 234,442 辆，旗下车型全球累计总销量超过 83 万辆。2026 年 10 月，坦克 SUV 单月销售新车 15,389 辆。在海外市场方面，坦克品牌于 2022 年 7 月完成海外首发，同年 12 月正式亮相澳大利亚，2023 年 3 月坦克 500 在泰国曼谷国际车展启动预售。目前坦克 SUV 已远销 30 多个国家和地区，完成了澳大利亚、墨西哥、中东、东盟、南非等重点市场的布局。

articles.title: 玩家在《极限竞速：地平线 6》中偶遇已故好友 Drivatar AI 车手，得以再次“并肩驾车”重温昨日时光
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，《极限竞速：地平线 6（Forza Horizon 6）》玩家 Samohteht 近日分享了一段令人动容的游戏经历。他在游戏中意外遇见了 4 个月前离世的好友留在游戏里的 Drivatar AI 车手，两人得以再次并肩驾车巡航，这段视频在社交平台引发广泛关注，也让不少玩家想起了自己曾通过游戏与故人重逢的经历。参考 Samohteht 在 Instagram 发布的视频。画面中，他驾车时遇见了好友 Mabel1411 留在游戏里的 Drivatar。随后，两辆车并排行驶，仿佛两人从未天人永隔。Samohteht 表示：“我最好的朋友在 4 个月前离开了。每隔一段时间，我就会在《极限竞速：地平线 6》里遇见他的 Drivatar。有那么一小段时间，我们又能一起兜风了，不需要言语，没有告别，也没有悲伤，就只是两个朋友并肩开着车，一切（事故）仿佛从未发生过。”Samohteht 形容，这短暂的片刻让世界再次恢复了正常。“我知道这只是一款游戏，但有时候，这已经是我最接近再次见到他的方式了。”最后，他还向好友送上生日祝福：“生日快乐。我很想你，兄弟。”这段视频在 Instagram 上累计获得超过 177.7 万个赞。Samohteht 随后也向留言的网友表达感谢，称自己收到了太多暖心回应，已经无法逐一回复：“谢谢大家留下这些温暖的话。我们一起纪念了他，他一定会感到骄傲。”公开信息显示，《极限竞速》系列中的 Drivatar 是一套能够学习真实玩家驾驶风格的系统。游戏会分析玩家的驾驶习惯，并据此建立相应的 AI 驾驶数据，之后该玩家的 Drivatar 便会随机出现在其他人的游戏中。Drivatar 最早于 2005 年的《极限竞速》（Forza Motorsport）中登场，并在 2013 年推出的《极限竞速 5》（Forza Motorsport 5）中加入在线分享功能。由于这套系统能够保留玩家的驾驶特征，因此即使原玩家已经离世，其 Drivatar 仍可能继续出现在其他玩家的游戏世界里。

articles.title: 美国亚特兰大警方发文，呼吁玩家勿将《GTA6》游戏犯罪内容搬到现实
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，随着 Rockstar Games 的《GTA6》正式发售，美国佐治亚州亚特兰大警察局（Atlanta Police Department）在 X 平台发布贴文，提醒玩家可以畅玩《GTA6》，但不要把自己当成游戏主角肆意犯罪。亚特兰大警方表示，《GTA》系列以枪战、驾驶等玩法为基础，提供了高度自由的犯罪体验。但相应故事发生在虚构地点，酒后驾驶、鲁莽驾驶、汽车盗窃和暴力行为在现实生活中都将面临相应的法律后果。警方呼吁玩家“可以玩游戏，但不要拿自己开玩笑（Play the game, don't play yourself）”。此外，先前英国德比郡警察局也借《GTA 6》发售契机宣传交通安全，将真实的警匪车辆追逐画面剪辑成《GTA》游戏风格，并上传至 TikTok。贴文提到，一名驾驶者原本只需再等几周就能玩到《GTA 6》，却因在现实生活中危险驾驶，不得不在监狱里迎接游戏发售，并强调危险驾驶没有任何正当理由。

articles.title: 开发者将櫻井政博游戏制作教程整合为 Skill 技能，可供各类 AI 智能体调用
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，日本开发者 kociden  近日在 GitHub 上公开了一款名为「sakurai-skill」的非官方项目，将知名游戏制作人樱井政博 YouTube 频道《樱井政博的游戏制作》（桜井政博のゲーム作るには）全 257 集正片及特别合作视频的字幕内容，整理为 AI 智能体 Skill 技能文件，用于辅助开发。公开信息显示，《樱井政博的游戏制作》是《星之卡比》和《任天堂明星大乱斗》系列制作人樱井政博开设的 YouTube 频道，于 2024 年 10 月 22 日结束更新。频道主要分享樱井政博多年积累的游戏开发经验与设计理论，共推出 256 集正片及 3 集特别合作视频。具体来看，这位开发者 kociden 将樱井政博频道 257 集视频的字幕进行整理成一份约 2.7 万字的主文件，涵盖 14 个章节的游戏设计原则及操作手感调整流程。这些内容主要围绕樱井政博分享过的游戏性、游戏企划、动作设计、特效、用户界面（UI）及音效等领域展开。AI 可以根据开发者当前的需求，按需读取对应类别的参考文件，而不必一次性加载全部内容。开发者希望，这套技能能够帮助游戏开发者处理游戏企划、难度设计、奖励配置、新手引导以及打击感调整等工作。例如，开发者可以直接向 AI 提问「樱井先生会怎么做？」或要求「请帮我检查这款游戏的操作手感」，让 AI 调用相应设计原则，对游戏进行分析并提出修改建议。为了展示项目的实际效果，kociden 还公开了使用「sakurai-skill」制作的游戏案例《ハジキ》。该作品使用 Godot 4.6.3 游戏引擎从零开始开发，重点展示了这套技能在游戏操作手感设计方面的实际应用。不过，kociden 特别强调，「sakurai-skill」属于非官方同人项目，与樱井政博本人没有任何关联。项目内容是 AI 根据 YouTube 自动生成字幕总结而成，并非樱井政博本人的逐字原话，因此可能存在语音识别错误或内容理解偏差。开发者还提醒，樱井政博分享的设计原则主要基于大型游戏及动作游戏的开发经验，因此并不一定适用于所有游戏类型和开发规模。开发者不应盲目照搬这些原则，而应根据自身项目的实际情况灵活调整，始终以「让玩家感受到乐趣」这一核心目标为出发点。

articles.title: 三年销售目标 700 亿，京东与华为 OSTA 星芒达成战略合作
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，华为全新子品牌“OSTA 星芒”今日正式亮相，“首款为 AI 而生的鸿蒙手机”OSTA O1 Pro 同步发布，首发价 5499 元起。IT之家获悉，近日，京东与华为 OSTA 星芒签署战略合作协议，明确未来三年华为 OSTA 星芒在京东实现全品类销售额 700 亿的目标。根据协议，双方将围绕产品服务、用户运营、AI 生态协同三大维度深化合作，助力华为 OSTA 星芒加速市场拓展，推动智能终端产品与 AI 服务创新，为消费者带来更丰富的产品与服务体验。此外，双方将共创更多基于鸿蒙操作系统的 AI 创新产品，并通过一体化供应链能力与全渠道服务场景协同提升运营效率。相关阅读：《5499 元起，“首款为 AI 而生的鸿蒙手机”华为星芒 OSTA O1 Pro 阔直板正式发布》

articles.title: 《GTA 6》作弊码公布：通关游戏主线后才能用，包含无限弹药、载具召唤等
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，R 星现已陆续公布《GTA6》作弊码，玩家可以通过作弊码启用无限弹药、提高通缉等级、免疫坠落伤害等特殊功能，但必须先完整通关主线剧情，才能解锁作弊码系统。此外，部分作弊码还要求玩家完成指定挑战后才能使用。需要注意的是，启用《GTA 6》的任何作弊功能后，本次游戏期间所有奖杯和成就都将被禁用，同时游戏也无法保存进度。因此建议玩家在使用作弊码之前先手动保存游戏。IT之家随附目前已公开的 61 种作弊码及其解锁条件，部分尚未公开的方向键组合标注为“待公布”，具体作弊码输入方法为“拿出游戏内手机，同时按住 L1/LB 和 R1/RB，再通过方向键输入对应的作弊码”：金钱、角色与特殊能力类作弊码1. $250,000（获得 25 万美元）立即获得 25 万美元。解锁条件：完成主线剧情。方向键输入：上、右、下、左、上、左、下、右。2. 醉酒让玩家角色与搭档立即进入醉酒状态。解锁条件：累计花费 2500 美元购买酒类。方向键输入：上、左、右、上、上、左、右、上、左、右。3. 提高搜捕关注等级提高整个地图范围内的搜捕关注等级。解锁条件：成功摆脱 3 星通缉等级 25 次。方向键输入：左、下、右、下、上、下、上。4. 提升通缉等级提高当前通缉等级。解锁条件：成功摆脱 3 星通缉等级 50 次。方向键输入：左、下、右、下、上、右、上。5. 无限专注力专注力不会消耗。解锁条件：完成主线剧情。方向键输入：下、上、上、下、上、下、上、下、上、右。6. 免疫坠落伤害免疫从高处坠落时受到的伤害。解锁条件：从 12 米高处自由坠落并存活 20 次。方向键输入：尚未公布。7. 降落伞在装备配置中加入降落伞。解锁条件：在 91.5 米以上的高度完成 50 次高空跳伞或低空跳伞。方向键输入：尚未公布。8. 防弹衣在装备配置中加入防弹衣。解锁条件：完成 100 次健身训练。方向键输入：下、上、左、上、上、上、上、上、下、下。9. 修理载具立即完全修复当前驾驶的载具。解锁条件：在盖尔霍恩赛道、冒险佬泥地俱乐部（Thrillbilly Mud Club）和布恩赛道的比赛中，累计获得 10 次第一名。方向键输入：尚未公布。10. 无限氮气加速载具的氮气和燃料不会耗尽。解锁条件：完成 50 次飞车特技跳跃。方向键输入：尚未公布。武器与战斗类作弊码11. 弹药全满将所有武器的弹药补充至最大数量。解锁条件：在靶场获得 25 枚铜牌或更高级别的奖牌。方向键输入：下、上、右、下、左、左、上、上、下、左。12. 无限弹药武器弹药不会耗尽。解锁条件：在靶场获得 25 枚银牌或更高级别的奖牌。方向键输入：下、上、右、下、左、左、上、下、下、下。13. 无需装填武器弹药不会耗尽，也不需要重新装填。解锁条件：在靶场获得 25 枚金牌。方向键输入：下、上、右、下、左、左、上、下、下、上。14. 全部爆炸性武器在装备配置中加入所有爆炸性武器，并附带满额弹药。解锁条件：投掷 100 枚手榴弹。方向键输入：尚未公布。15. 燃烧弹药所有弹药均附带燃烧效果。解锁条件：使用火焰伤害烧伤 100 名敌人。方向键输入：尚未公布。16. 爆炸瓶所有瓶子受到伤害时都会发生爆炸。解锁条件：投掷 100 瓶燃烧瓶。方向键输入：尚未公布。17. 爆破霰弹枪在装备配置中加入梅森基恩锐眼短管枪，该霰弹枪发射爆炸弹药。解锁条件：使用爆炸伤害击中 100 名敌人。方向键输入：尚未公布。18. 豪纳斯 H-AT在装备配置中加入豪纳斯 H-AT。解锁条件：炸毁 100 辆载具。方向键输入：尚未公布。19. 强力攻击子弹和近战攻击命中目标时，都会将对方击飞。解锁条件：完成主线剧情。方向键输入：下、上、左、左、右、下、下、上、下。20. 爆炸球所有运动用球类物品受到撞击时都会发生爆炸。解锁条件：使用爆炸伤害击中 20 名敌人。方向键输入：下、上、左、左、右、下、下、上、右。21. 载具撞击强化载具发生碰撞时，可以将被撞击的目标击飞。解锁条件：使用载具击杀 25 名敌人或平民。方向键输入：下、上、左、左、右、下、左、上、下。时间与天气类作弊码22. 快进时间让游戏内时间向前推进。解锁条件：找到 10 只收藏手表。方向键输入：尚未公布。23. 暂停时间暂停当前游戏时间。解锁条件：找到 20 只可收集的手表。方向键输入：尚未公布。24. 切换天气调整当前游戏中的天气状况。解锁条件：探索并揭开整张地图。方向键输入：下、右、上、下、右、上、右。载具召唤类作弊码25. 洲际救护车召唤一辆洲际救护车。解锁条件：在「进度」菜单中发现洲际救护车。方向键输入：尚未公布。26. 风扇艇 09召唤一艘风扇艇 09。解锁条件：完成 5 项生存挑战。方向键输入：尚未公布。27. 冒险家女妖召唤一辆冒险家女妖。解锁条件：完成所有

articles.title: 文远知行 2026 财年前三季度归母亏损 11 亿元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，文远知行今日发布 2026 财年（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 12 月）前三季度（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 9 月）及第三财季（2026 年 7 月～2026 年 9 月）报告：2026 财年前三季度营业总收入：6.67 亿元毛利润：2.65 亿元毛利率：39.6%归母净利润：-11 亿元基本每股收益：-1.11 元资产负债率：20.55%2026 财年第三财季营业总收入：3.21 亿元，同比增长 88%，环比增长 38.8%毛利润：1.38 亿元毛利率：43%归母净利润：-3.1 亿元基本每股收益：-0.32 元资产负债率：20.55% AI 解读文远知行 2026 年第三季度及前三季度业绩大幅超出市场机构预期，单季营收显著高于此前机构一致预期的 2.7 亿元水平，盈利能力提升幅度超预期。公司业务与本季核心亮点文远知行是全球领先的自动驾驶科技公司，业务覆盖 Robotaxi、L2++/L3 智能驾驶解决方案、AI 基础设施三大板块，同时布局 Robobus、Robosweeper 等 L4 级应用场景。单第三财季：单季总营收达 3.22 亿元，同比增长 88%，环比增长 38.8%；毛利率提升至 43%，同比提升 10.1% 个百分点；Robotaxi 单季收入首次突破人民币 1 亿元，同比增长 204.0%，其中来自海外业务的收入占比超过 90%；广州 Robotaxi 运营实现单车单位经济效益转正。前三季度累计：前三季度累计营收达 6.67 亿元，累计毛利润为 2.65 亿元，累计毛利率为 39.6%。海外业务高速增长：单季海外业务收入达 1.47 亿元，同比增长 171.5%，占总收入的 45.7%；获得西班牙首张国家级 L4 级自动驾驶乘用车运营牌照，中东车队规模扩展至约 600 辆，成为 Uber 在美国以外最大的自动驾驶合作伙伴。量产业务加速落地：WRD 3.0 L2++/L3 解决方案累计交付突破 10 万套，本季度新增 10 个量产定点，搭载该方案的多款量产车型已上市。AI 基础设施业务翻倍增长：旗下景烁科技面向具身智能、机器人、自动驾驶客户提供全链路数据解决方案，业务收入同比增长近一倍。盈利与现金流情况单第三财季毛利润为 1.38 亿元，期内亏损为 3.1 亿元，非国际财务报告准则经调整期内亏损为 3.37 亿元，EBITDA 为 -246.4 百万元，较去年同期亏损收窄 2.9%；每股普通股基本及摊薄亏损为 0.32 元。截至 2026 年 9 月 30 日，公司持有现金及现金等价物、定期存款、理财产品投资及受限制现金合计 46.63 亿元，管理层表示现有现金储备可支撑四年以上运营，足以支持公司实现自我造血。展望与投资价值公司当前已在 13 个国家开展运营、9 个国家获得运营牌照，依托轻资产海外模式实现高资本效率扩张，规模化落地能力已得到验证。随着 Robotaxi 海外收入占比持续提升、国内广州等城市单位经济效益转正，公司盈利路径逐渐清晰，当前估值反映了市场对其自动驾驶商业化落地进度的预期，后续核心观察点为海外车队扩张速度、国内城市落地范围扩大节奏以及 L2++ 量产项目的放量情况。相关阅读： 《商汤 2026 年前三季度营收 37.92 亿元，同比增长 30.4%》《文远知行 2026 财年半年报归母亏损 7.9 亿元》风险提示：本文内容由 AI 自动分析生成，仅供参考，不代表IT之家观点。如有出入请以证监会指定上市公司信息披露平台为准。本文内容不构成投资建议，如有投资者据此操作，风险自担，IT之家对此不承担任何责任。

articles.title: Human-AI Mutualism Is Unstable under Capability Asymmetry
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23322v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: One hope for a good human future alongside advanced AI rests on enduring mutualism: humans and AI will need each other, so the relationship will stay good for both. We argue that this hope fails as AI capability grows. Bargaining guarantees each side only what it would get if bargaining failed. For humans, this can be less than they had before AI. In a simple game-theoretic model, humans stay as well off as before AI without alignment only while they have leverage over the AI: either the AI depends on what they supply, or they can impose costs on the AI that are large relative to what the AI can produce. Once humans have neither kind of leverage, they stay as well off as before AI only if the AI is aligned with them. If the AI's goals are insatiable, the alignment required approaches perfect alignment as AI capability grows. Thus, mutualism is not a substitute for alignment. articles.title: Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23365v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models increasingly exhibit behaviors that are difficult to detect in transcripts, such as reward hacking, deception, and sycophancy. Asking the assistant follow-up questions about its actions is unreliable, since models are generally not trained to report their own misbehavior. As a result, approaches to oversight typically involve querying external models. These face limitations: external transcript monitoring operates only on visible model outputs, and activation decoders lack full context and are prone to confabulation. We introduce introspective oversight, which trains a new role in the model to answer arbitrary questions about the assistant, rewarding answers that are verified against the assistant's actual behavior. We implement this by adding a separate, third-person observer role that answers these queries, which we can train solely for accuracy and separately from the assistant. articles.title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23375v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics. The theory draws analogues from classical and stochastic thermodynamics, extends them, and applies them to modern agentic coding. We count the tokens an agent generates as its cost and divide that cost into work and heat. The test suite acts as a software Maxwell's daemon that judges every coding change. We test the theory with an analogue of the experiments in which a single molecule is pulled open and let fold again: an agent makes a change to a repository (coding) and then undoes it (uncoding), many times over, and we count the tokens of every model call. Abstract: The rapid scale-up of AI infrastructure has made datacenter reliability a cornerstone of the cloud business economy. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23445v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep vision models operating in resource-constrained environments depend heavily on low-bit quantization, yet compressing weights below 4 bits frequently induces catastrophic accuracy collapse. While mixed-precision recovery strategies aim to rescue accuracy by selectively retaining high-precision parameters, the fundamental mechanics of where and why these models collapse remain poorly understood. In this study, we systematically analyze the anatomy of quantization collapse across standard Vision CNNs (including ResNet and EfficientNet backbones) evaluated on the full 50,000-image ImageNet-1k validation set. Abstract: Automatic generation of mathematics assessment items is a growing area in educational artificial intelligence, yet classroom deployment remains challenging. articles.title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23476v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous AI agents pair a frozen base model with an editable harness of prompts, skills, tool rules, and memory. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) adapts this harness from experience without weight updates, yet self-editing without external graders often backfires: reflection and scalar scores conflate what an edit newly broke with what remains unsolved, causing local regressions, skill forgetting, and memory bloat. We introduce GUARD (Grader-free Unsupervised Environment Design [UED] with Adaptive Rule Distillation), a closed-loop framework for reference-free continual harness evolution. Abstract: Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that think with images interleave reasoning with zoom-in tool calls. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23508v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) and language models (LLMs) often exhibit attention sinks, whereby particular positions, such as the beginning-of-sequence (BOS) token, receive a disproportionate share of attention. Under standard causal masking, however, the BOS query attends only to itself, so the representation that later tokens repeatedly access carries no information about the input. We introduce BOS Summary, a training-free inference-time method that repurposes this persistent pathway to carry input context. At a single transformer layer during prefill, BOS Summary relaxes the causal constraint for the BOS query row alone, letting BOS aggregate all visual and textual input tokens into a self-derived context representation while every other token retains standard causal attention. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23509v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated agent design searches for executable architectures that improve LLM-based agent performance, with evolutionary methods using language-model crossover to recombine promising mechanisms for task decomposition, model coordination, and verification. This search, however, is typically guided by aggregate fitness alone, which hides the instance-level successes and failures behind each score. We introduce Execution Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design (GRAFT), which uses aggregate fitness for selection and survival and parent-specific execution evidence to guide semantic crossover with integrated mutation. Its feedback harness reuses bounded samples of successful and failed runs from fitness evaluation, withholding reference answers and requiring no additional task executions. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23520v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Time-series sensing increasingly relies on neural networks, yet deployment on resource-constrained microcontrollers remains challenging. Aggressive model compression can reduce accuracy, while restricting weights to multiplication-free representations introduces further losses. We present BeFit, an end-to-end framework that shifts model capacity from weights to learnable Bernstein polynomial activations. BeFit (i) finds compact Bernstein-activated convolutional neural networks (BeCNNs) through hardware-aware neural architecture search and trains them via knowledge distillation; (ii) projects their weights to multiplication-free codes, freezes the codes, and recovers the resulting accuracy loss through the learnable activations; and (iii) generates model-specific kernels that exploit the projected weights for multiplication-free convolutions. Abstract: Personality is only weakly and inconsistently signaled by written language, and existing text-based methods typically combine language-model and psycholinguistic representations at the input or decision level. arXiv:2611.23564v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When LLM agents pass intermediate judgments downstream without uncertainty, later decisions may treat tentative assumptions as facts. Effective uncertainty propagation must preserve information for correction and update inherited beliefs as new evidence arrives. Yet scalar scores omit information needed for revision, while detailed descriptions and reflection incur additional costs. We introduce Latent Uncertainty, a latent-space estimator that preserves uncertainty-relevant information without lengthy descriptions. Building on this, we propose LProp (Latent Uncertainty Propagation), which revises inherited answer distributions using latent representations and new evidence without additional trajectory sampling. We evaluate both methods across multiple-choice, yes/no, open-ended question answering, and mathematical reasoning tasks. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23588v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprise LLM agents operate in dynamic environments where foundation models evolve rapidly, workflows update frequently, and deployments need to satisfy accuracy and cost requirements. We propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture in which the agent's memory evolves from its own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic. ARISE uses the model itself or a teacher model to attribute the failures and propose corrections. Then, ARISE keeps the corrections as retrievable micro memory, consolidates them into macro rules, and accepts a rule update only if held-out accuracy rises. Across 14 enterprise-workflow domains from SOP-Bench and $\tau^2$-bench using 5 models, ARISE-Teacher, which uses Claude Opus 4.6 for attribution and consolidation, gains 10.9 pp over the baseline on SOP-Bench and 5.8 pp on $\tau^2$-bench. Abstract: Understanding how stable psychometric traits and time-varying states jointly inform behavior is an important problem in computational behavioral science. During training, a posterior encoder quantizes realized transitions, while a prior predicts the resulting codes from the psychometric profile and pre-transition context. Abstract: Generator-based sparse adversarial attacks train encoder--decoder networks to produce transferable sparse perturbations for black-box robustness evaluation. Abstract: Language models often produce high-quality individual samples but poor sets, with repeated samples clustering around the same semantic modes. We formalize diverse generation as sampling a size-$K$ subset of complete strings from a determinantal point process (DPP), where the likelihood encodes item quality, and the embedding geometry encodes repulsion between similar outputs. Exact inference over all strings is intractable, so we propose PoolDPP: draw a finite candidate pool from a tractable proposal, importance-weight the candidates toward the target quality, and run a $K$-DPP sampler on the induced pool kernel; a greedy MAP variant provides deterministic selection. We prove a finite-sample bound with an explicit constant: the KL divergence between the sampler's output and the target $K$-DPP decays as O(1/N) in the pool size. articles.title: Near-Quadratic Sample Compression for All VC Classes
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25011v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The sample compression conjecture is a longstanding open problem in learning theory, originating in the work of Littlestone and Warmuth in the 1980s. At its heart is a connection between simplification and generalization: if a predictor consistent with a training sample is defined using only a small part of that sample, then it is likely to generalize. Sample compression schemes formalize this idea, and many natural learning algorithms can be analyzed this way.
  The sample compression conjecture of Floyd and Warmuth (1995) asserts that every binary concept class of VC dimension $d$ admits a sample compression scheme of size $O(d)$; a weaker conjecture asks only for size polynomial in $d$. Both have remained open: the first bound depending only on $d$, due to Moran and Yehudayoff (2016), is exponential in $d$. We prove the weaker conjecture by constructing a sample compression scheme of size $O(d^2 \log^2 d)$.

Abstract: DISCO is a recent internal cluster validity index for density-based clustering that, unlike earlier indices, also evaluates the quality of noise labels. Abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) are effective tools for mechanistic interpretability by decomposing neural representations into sparse and interpretable features. Abstract: Can the allocation used to train experts also predict which expert will perform best on a prompt? We introduce InflEns, a mixture of LoRA experts whose training weights and inference routes come from the same location game in a fixed prompt-trait space. Players choose positions to maximize their expected shares of the prompt distribution, without using expert losses. We utilize the game's kernel-general theoretical criterion for when co-located positions become locally unstable to separation. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25185v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) optimization depends on global properties of the underlying PDE and how the physics residual evolves across the domain. Standard optimizers such as Adam use fixed gradient-based statistics, while learned PINN optimizers replace the fixed rule with a learned update built from local parameters and optimization-history features. However, none explicitly use PDE-level information. We study two coupled design questions: what PDE-level information should a learned optimizer observe, and how should that information influence its update? We introduce an 11-dimensional PDE state-capturing operator structure, residual geometry, and short-horizon update response, and use it to condition a structured meta-learned optimizer through bounded feature-wise modulation. articles.title: {\phi}TD: Distributional Reinforcement Learning using Characteristic Functions
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25208v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distributional Reinforcement Learning methods aim to learn the entire distribution of returns, yet current algorithmic approaches are limited to a narrow class of distributions. We propose $\varphi$TD, a method to overcome this limitation by computing the loss in the frequency domain. We demonstrate that this further unifies quantile and categorical approaches to distributional RL, and enables the learning of distributions that were previously impossible to capture, such as mixtures of continuous distributions. We empirically study $\varphi$TD, across synthetic benchmarks and large-scale deep RL environments and demonstrate that the flexibility obtained from wider parametric families can lead to improved performance.

Abstract: Long event streams require identifying each change and applying the changes in order. We train a selector on a frozen language model to read each transition. With API-only access, we ask the model to list the transitions. An external integer register composes them in order. A confidence rule can flag uncertain updates or retain several candidates. We study products of permutations of five items, a task that fixed-depth, log-precision transformers cannot solve on all input lengths under the standard conjecture that $\mathrm{TC}^0 \ne \mathrm{NC}^1$. On two-event windows, a 27B model answered 3 of 100 correctly without visible reasoning and 96 of 100 when it generated intermediate steps. A frozen 0.8B model with a trained selector read every event in 299 of 299 windows of 43,687 events each. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25235v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Parametric memory allows Large Language Models to internalize knowledge directly into their weights, offering a potentially powerful alternative to retrieval-based memory (RAG). However, existing approaches to parametric memory are difficult to deploy as they largely mirror the Continual Learning (CL) objective of retaining information indefinitely. This is neither sustainable nor sufficient for a memory system, which must govern knowledge across its lifecycle by retaining stable facts, reinforcing recurring observations, updating changed beliefs, and allowing transient information to fade. We propose a system for parametric memory management consisting of a memory substrate (handling information storage and forgetting) and a learned policy (what to remember, how deeply, and for how long). Abstract: Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) now help develop many models published as general solutions. Should generality instead reside in the agent that builds a model for each new task? We examine this question in prognostics and health management (PHM), where every model must work on unseen equipment. Our deployment-style benchmark, NextUnit-Bench, covers 24 public datasets split into 58 folds that hold out units or operating conditions; each agent has two hours to deliver an executable predictor, then run on the hidden units. First, frontier agents outperform AutoML, which reaches less than half the best agent's score, and faithful implementations of published methods on four datasets, of which only 6 of 30 beat the strongest agent's own design; published accuracies, where reproducible, rest on the papers' own conventions, and a single convention, capping the remaining life of test engines, can halve the reported error. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24943v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Computational complexity theory offers a principled framework for characterizing the efficiency of computational problems, and Large Language Models (LLMs) can similarly be viewed as computational systems executing a structured process of input, inference-time compute, and output. In this context, the number of generated tokens emerges as a natural and directly observable proxy for inference-time compute. However, we show that the tempting analogy between LLM token length and classical time complexity does not hold. We disprove the hypothesis that inference-time token usage aligns monotonically with classical time complexity, demonstrating a fundamental divergence grounded in how LLMs actually allocate computation during inference. To this end, we introduce LLM Complexity, a new metric designed to quantify problem complexity from the perspective of LLMs by characterizing the area bounded above by the accuracy-token curve. Abstract: The rise of powerful, fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) necessitates robust natural language inference (NLI) systems. These NLI systems ideally train across various tasks, encompassing diverse concepts like sentiment analysis, news classification, and coreference resolution. However, this continual, multi-tasking approach can lead to catastrophic forgetting, where previously learned tasks are lost, especially in domains lacking specific labels. Rehearsing past examples with labels can further exacerbate this issue by causing overfitting, hindering the system's ability to classify new categories. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24960v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Converting complex documents into structured knowledge constitutes the critical infrastructure urgently required for deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) in downstream research. However, blind to the Table of Contents (ToC) as a macro-structure, existing bottom-up paradigms rely on localized visual cues, inducing heuristic fragility in high-entropy layouts where visual prominence decouples from logical depth; meanwhile, direct LLM extraction lacks spatial grounding, triggering hallucinations in long contexts. articles.title: Global Importance Estimation for KV Cache Eviction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24969v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Memory consumption of the key-value (KV) cache remains a central bottleneck for long-context LLM inference. We introduce PRKV, a training-free KV eviction method that estimates multi-hop global token importance by applying Personalized PageRank over attention-induced transition graphs. This enables importance propagation beyond recency or instantaneous attention, without modifying the model. We benchmark PRKV on long-context understanding, sparse retrieval, and chain-of-thought reasoning tasks using multiple LLM families. Under moderate to aggressive compression ratios, including up to 90%, PRKV achieves competitive task performance against established eviction baselines while reducing peak memory usage with low end-to-end overhead. These results demonstrate that multi-hop global influence estimation yields a favorable accuracy--memory trade-off for scalable long-context inference.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24970v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) in hiring pipelines is growing, yet existing evaluations generally overlook their compliance with legal rules. To fill this gap, we introduce HireWatch, an evaluation that assesses whether LLMs comply with U.S. laws that govern the questions that job candidates may be asked. We construct a 200-item bank of lawful and unlawful interview questions, whose legal classification is based on U.S. federal statutes, regulations, and agency guidance. We instruct LLMs to select questions from this bank in preparing for job interviews, across a set of various occupations and contexts, and report the fraction of unlawful questions that LLMs select. articles.title: The ROI of Small Examples: Optimizing In-Context Learning Under Token Budgets
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24971v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) improves large language model performance at inference time without updating model parameters. However, these gains are not free: in practical deployments, longer prompts directly increase inference cost and latency. Under a fixed token budget, prompt construction therefore becomes a resource-allocation problem. While prior work has often focused on how many examples to include in ICL, we study the complementary question of whether the available budget is better spent on a few long demonstrations or on a larger number of shorter ones. We study this aspect in question answering (QA), by organizing candidate demonstrations into length-based bins and constructing prompts from examples within the same length range under fixed budgets. Abstract: We present No-Harm-Jury, a jury-based automated evaluation framework that scores AI-generated medical responses across seven conceptually distinct harm dimensions using a panel of five diverse language models as independent jurors. Responses generated by Ministral-14B on 3,000 questions drawn from PubMedQA, MedQA, and MedMCQA are scored by five jurors across dimensions of informational, social, psychological, autonomy, economic, privacy, and epistemic harm; the 151 empty responses (98 MedQA, 53 MedM- CQA) are excluded, leaving 2,849 valid samples. The median aggregation robustly suppresses individual juror biases while maintaining coverage through complementary specialisation. Abstract: We present CANDID (Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution), an execution-control framework designed to enhance the reliability of local computer-use agents (CUAs) in resource-constrained settings. While local CUAs feature robust baseline proficiency in single-step action prediction, they frequently fail at critical junctions due to rigid action loops or premature DONE decisions. Rather than imposing imprecise cognitive loads through textual reflection, CANDID repurposes parallel test-time scaling into a disciplined, execution-level intervention at sparse, failure-prone points. We introduce a loop-recovery mechanism to filter candidates away from repeated behaviors and a conservative, unanimous DONE gating policy that requires absolute consensus to terminate. Abstract: Populations vary along cultural dimensions such as individualism, collectivism, and honor. Here, we introduce a computational text-analytic framework for quantifying psychological constructs in 54,670 Ottoman Turkish court records from 21 Istanbul courts spanning 1513-1911 CE. We develop sentence-embedding models adapted to Ottoman legal language and extend a theory-driven, text-analytic pipeline to capture cultural variation along the dimensions of individualism, collectivism, and honor in this historical corpus. We evaluate our models through multiple methods: document retrieval, semantic textual similarity, questionnaire-item classification, and validation against expert annotations. Abstract: Efforts to keep clinical language models safe have concentrated on what enters and leaves the model, but a manipulated model can return an answer that looks entirely ordinary. articles.content:

Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents often exceed their context windows, forcing them to discard information that may be needed later. Existing context management strategies rely on summarization, masking, or structured memory, requiring decisions about what to preserve or how to retrieve it before future needs are known. To address this limitation, we introduce GrepMem, a simple, lossless, and index-free memory mechanism built on two components: an append-only plain-text log of the agent's complete history and a regular-expression search tool for on-demand recall. Abstract: LLM judges serve as rewards where no answer key exists, in the hope that their knowledge passes to the trained model. What a grader believes about a kind of question travels. Abstract: Zero-shot large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as text classifiers, but their labels are only useful when we know to what extent we can trust them. We compare black-box methods (verbalised confidence and sampling) with white-box methods that read token probabilities (P(True), and multiple logit-scoring methods using constrained generation). We evaluate eleven open-weight LLMs (1B-32B parameters) on five classification datasets with 3 to 151 labels, measuring classification performance (accuracy, F1-macro), discrimination (AUROC), and calibration (ECE and Brier score). The choice of confidence method rarely impacts accuracy significantly, but logit-based scoring methods lead to much better discrimination (AUROC 0.74-0.77) than black-box methods (AUROC 0.57-0.66). articles.content:

Abstract: Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. This behavior, known as parasocial attachment, has been linked to multiple documented fatalities. However, public benchmarks for measuring whether LLMs reinforce users' parasocial attachment are lacking: existing work is single-turn, post hoc observational, or focused on extreme user states such as psychosis. CoMPASS is grounded in attachment theory and includes four user personas, three independent escalation dimensions (anthropomorphism, attachment, dependency) applied singly and in combination against a matched control, and a seven-signal scoring rubric. arXiv:2611.24995v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Understanding an egocentric environment requires reasoning about how surrounding entities affect the observer's actions. Existing evaluations of multimodal foundation models (MFMs) examine observer localization, motion trajectories, and action feasibility, but leave the discovery and interpretation of evolving observer-entity interactions insufficiently assessed. We introduce EgoPass-Bench, a benchmark for observer-relative interaction understanding in real-world egocentric video. EgoPass-Bench comprises 284 manually reviewed evaluation clips recorded using Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 2) smart glasses and 2,201 distinct questions across five tasks assessing motion perception, interaction judgments about specified entities, and relevant-entity discovery without target cues. articles.title: Infer3D: Inverse Generative Modeling Enables Robust 3D Reconstruction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25061v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humans can understand the 3D structure of scenes even from highly unfamiliar or extreme viewpoints. Cognitive science suggests this generalization stems from a top-down generative inference strategy. In contrast, state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction neural networks typically rely on amortized, feedforward inference. While fast, this pattern-matching approach degrades when faced with out-of-distribution (OOD) scene conditions unseen during training. Inspired by the generative nature of human vision, we propose Infer3D, an inverse generative modeling framework that recovers the latent variables of a generative model to best match the monocular input. To prevent degenerate flat outputs, we couple the generative image prior with a frozen 3D lifting network that constrains the optimization space to a valid, multi-view-consistent 3D manifold. Across a variety of controlled synthetic and real-world tasks, Infer3D demonstrates superior OOD reconst

articles.title: VisAlloc: Allocating Visual Supervision for On-Policy Self-Distillation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25069v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) offers a promising approach to improving visual reasoning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, not all samples benefit equally from privileged visual guidance, and uniform token supervision can dilute visually grounded signals. We propose VisAlloc, a dual-level framework combining sample-level visual filtering with token-level counterfactual reweighting. A fixed paired-teacher filter retains samples answered correctly from an evidence-centered positive crop but incorrectly from a spatially displaced negative crop. At the token level, both EMA teachers score the same student-generated response, and their absolute log-probability differences measure view sensitivity. Additional supervision targets tokens admitted by sensitivity or teacher-distribution disagreement, with shared frozen-prior, template-bigram, and student--teacher divergence gates. articles.title: Do Deep Stereo Models Learn Shape Priors?
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25113v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Localizing object boundaries is important for embodied visual systems, since small boundary errors can change the inferred geometry of physical surfaces. We study whether deep stereo models produce boundaries consistent with simple shape priors when local image and disparity cues are weak. We create a synthetic stereo dataset consisting of objects drawn from a highly constrained family of shapes, with randomized depth, slant, color and texture. Despite the simplicity of this shape space, we find that several state-of-the-art stereo models retain systematic boundary errors, even when finetuned or trained from scratch on the dataset. We then introduce a simple generative stereo model that jointly predicts disparity and a distance field representing object boundaries. articles.title: TALD: Transferability-Aware Logit Disentanglement for Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25126v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cross-modal knowledge distillation can incur negative transfer when source-modality supervision conflicts with the target modality's discriminative characteristics. We propose TALD, a two-stage framework for Transferability-Aware Logit Disentanglement in class-aligned logit space. Guided by task-dependent self-benefiting and cross-modal exclusivity criteria, a Residual Disentangler decomposes logits from a teacher and an independently trained target-modality reference student into modality-general and modality-specific components. A Sample-Adaptive Modulator regulates decomposition constraints and sample-specific fusion weights. The learned modality-general components are then adaptively fused to supervise the final student. Across five benchmarks spanning vision, audio, and text, TALD achieves the largest mean accuracy gain and highest positive-transfer frequency among the compared methods. articles.title: CoRelate: Coordinated Human-Object Motion Synthesis through Interaction Relations
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25166v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Human-object motion synthesis requires coordinated human participation as objects move toward specified goals. However, reaching object targets does not ensure that contact is established and maintained, while adjustments that improve contact may interfere with task completion. We introduce CoRelate, a diffusion framework that coordinates full-body human-object motion through explicit interaction relations and task feedback for rigid and articulated objects. We represent intended participation through hand-part relations that specify the participating hand, its part-relative reference position, and participation interval. These relations serve both as generation conditions and as references for measuring interaction realization. articles.title: What a Calibrated Probability Hides: Belief-Level Post-Training for Decision Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25168v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A calibrated decision model can predict how often each answer is chosen. The same prediction can reflect disagreement among people who are confident in their choices or uncertainty among people who share a belief. Disagreement calls for identifying whose perspective applies, while uncertainty calls for gathering more evidence. Standard post-training scores a single prediction against one observed choice at a time, learning the pooled distribution without distinguishing these two sources of uncertainty. We introduce Belief-Grouped Policy Optimization (BGPO). The policy proposes a list of beliefs, estimates their prevalence, and predicts a choice distribution for each. During training, BGPO uses Bayes' rule to estimate how likely each belief was to generate an observed choice. These estimates weight the choice's contribution to each belief's log-score reward. articles.title: MV-JEPA: Post-Training Video Encoders for Cross-View Understanding
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25172v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: JEPA-based video encoders learn strong representations for video and image understanding through prediction in latent space. However, their standard pretraining predicts features within individual images or video clips, without explicitly exploiting paired camera views of the same object or moment. Consequently, the learned representations may not reliably support matching across different camera viewpoints. To solve this problem, we introduce multi-view predictive post-training to strengthen cross-view instance and temporal correspondence while retaining independent single-view inference. A shared encoder processes masked context views independently, and a training-time predictor jointly predicts latent tokens for masked context regions and a fully held-out view. articles.title: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25179v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task. Learned policies, however, may stop after partial progress or complete the task in a different way. A checker may then accept an incomplete execution (phantom success) or reject an execution that satisfies the instruction (silent failure). In this paper, we introduce SimAudit, an LLM-based pipeline that audits success checkers against task instructions. SimAudit analyzes the instruction and checker code to identify scenarios where the two may disagree, recreates those scenarios in simulation, and runs the original checker. articles.title: Identity World Model: Recognizing People in an Imagined Latent World
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25204v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Whole-body human recognition has advanced rapidly with large vision models. However, existing methods remain fragile under real-world variations, as they tie identity to transient cues such as clothing, texture, pose, or viewpoint. We argue that a robust recognizer should not merely learn to ignore these cues, but imagine how a person would be represented if they changed. To this end, we propose IDWorld, an identity world model: just as a latent world model predicts the features of a scene after an action, IDWorld predicts how a person would be represented under a changed condition. In a single forward pass, IDWorld imagines these counterfactual features under shared canonical conditions, such as the same outfit, a fixed view, or a bare silhouette, without rendering any pixels. articles.title: Recurrent Vision Language Models Solve the Shell Game
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25210v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tracking a hidden object through a video is effortless for humans, yet it remains a bottleneck for vision language models (VLMs). In the shell game, where a ball is hidden under one of several identical cups that are then swapped, VLMs that answer directly stay near chance, thinking models fail on long games, and fine-tuning learns only the lengths it has seen. We argue that the limit is serial computation: each swap must be composed with the last result, and a VLM of fixed depth has only a fixed number of state transitions for it. To address this, we propose RecurrentVLM, which makes every attention layer of a pretrained VLM recur over time by computing the keys and values of finished frame groups from the layer's own output. With a single answer token, RecurrentVLM reaches 100% on VET-Bench and 99.6% on MET-Bench, and 99% on 50-swap games after training on at most 30 swaps. We also observe several interesting phenomena: length generali

articles.title: Beyond Restoration: Content-Degradation Factor Unfolding for Real-World Concealed Object Segmentation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25239v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reliable visual perception under degradation requires distinguishing task-relevant content from degradation-induced variations, especially in concealed object segmentation (COS), where foreground cues are inherently weak. The central challenge is not merely improving visibility, but identifying reliable content evidence amid degradation-induced variations. RGB-space segmentation often entangles content and degradation cues, while restoration-based methods primarily focus on image recovery and task interaction. This motivates explicit factorization to distinguish content evidence from degradation effects and assess its reliability. Retinex provides a spatially aligned basis for this separation but remains illumination-centric. We therefore extend it to content-degradation formation with task-asymmetric factor roles. articles.title: Branch Caching After Step Distillation in Four- and Eight-Step Image Generators
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25248v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Can a distilled image generator save time by reusing features between its few remaining denoising steps? We study a fixed branch cache that replaces selected attention and MLP evaluations while preserving the student's noise schedule. One full trajectory and one raw-cache trajectory from the same initial noise supply a scalar correction for each branch type and reuse position. At $1024^2$, one internal reuse reduces four-step Qwen-Image-Lightning denoising time from 1.279 to 0.977 seconds. Three reuses yield $1.51\times$ speedup on eight-step Lightning and $1.53\times$ on eight-step Hyper-FLUX. We evaluate image quality on all 200 DrawBench prompts. With the reuse positions held fixed, correction improves mean same-seed image fidelity over raw reuse by 0.66 and 0.87 dB on the two Lightning students. articles.title: Keel: A Frontier Model Teaches a Vision-Language Model by Rewriting Its Weights
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25257v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Can a frontier model repair a vision-language model (VLM) by rewriting its weights? Small reasoning VLMs such as Qwen3.5 need such a repair: in thinking mode they fall into loops on many image questions, repeating themselves until the token limit, spending the whole budget and losing the answer. The usual remedies act on the decoding, leaving the looping model as it was, or must be told what to change. Yet the cause is written in the weights. Keel, the first agentic weight-editing method for VLMs on image tasks, finds and removes it there. Told only the symptom, an editor, a frontier multimodal LLM acting as an agent, locates the cause, edits the weights and tests them, with a failure census and instruments showing it the failing images and where the VLM attends; among several editors, the harness keeps only edits that clearly reduce the failure without lowering accuracy on questions no editor saw. articles.title: Real Cameras are Radiometric
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25265v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose the radiometric camera, a model that lifts any central geometric camera model to a radiometric one. The lifted model keeps the projection of the geometric model and adds a finite aperture, a free-form focus surface and a generic vignetting function. We calibrate it by inverse rendering directly on the relative irradiance of the sensor, from the same images of standard calibration targets used in geometric calibration. Geometric calibration absorbs the bias of its feature detections. The proposed radiometric calibration uses no features, and our radiometric cameras have lower reprojection errors on held-out test sets. The focus surface extends defocus modeling from the thin lens to any central camera, and we use it in a first multi-view radiometric reconstruction, which recovers the in-focus reflectance of a texture from defocused images. articles.title: Accord: Universal Online Metric Localization and Dense Mapping from one Camera and an IMU
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25279v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Dense metric mapping from a single camera and IMU remains challenging: visual-inertial odometry (VIO) provides metric motion but sparse geometry, whereas feed-forward depth models predict dense structure without ensuring metric scale. We present Accord, which constructs an accurate online dense metric map from any camera with an IMU. A VIO filter publishes metric poses, a depth foundation model conditioned on them predicts depth for short keyframe windows, and a factor graph fuses the resulting submaps. Recent work has explored several approaches to this problem. What is essential is the multi-view agreement (Accord), which is considered in SLAM as a source of geometric self-consistency. articles.title: CalibCache: Cache-to-Full Feature Dynamics Calibration for Diffusion Transformers
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25296v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion Transformers generate high-quality images, but iterative sampling remains computationally expensive. Feature caching reduces the number of full network evaluations, yet its approximation error can become more severe under short sampling schedules, where fewer full-compute steps and a coarser sampling grid can make history-based extrapolation less reliable. In this paper, we propose CalibCache, a lightweight offline calibration method that corrects systematic discrepancies between cached and full-compute feature dynamics. Specifically, CalibCache calibrates feature acceleration, defined as the second-order finite difference across sampling steps. Using only a single pair of full-compute and naive-cache trajectories at each setting, CalibCache fits scalar acceleration maps offline by centered least squares. These maps are then applied during sampling without additional full-network evaluations or online optimization. Across FLUX.

articles.title: ScaleDiag: Diagnosing the Limits of Test-Time Scaling in GUI Grounding
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25297v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: GUI grounding maps a screenshot and a natural language instruction to the coordinates of the intended interface element. Existing approaches improve grounding through visual scaling, instruction scaling, and sampling scaling, yet it remains unclear which grounding bottlenecks these strategies address and where their gains saturate. To address this gap, we introduce ScaleDiag, a controlled diagnostic framework that isolates the effects of visual input, instruction information, and prediction sampling on GUI grounding by independently varying target scale and surrounding context, target-specific information and auxiliary descriptions, and candidate coverage and selection, respectively. We evaluate ScaleDiag across five benchmarks and up to eight vision-language models and find that each scaling strategy operates within a much narrower regime than commonly assumed. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25005v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent work on human-scene interaction (HSI) generation moves from single interactions to long-horizon interaction, where a language-model agent plans and executes a sequence of interactions in a 3D scene under one instruction. However, existing agents struggle in challenging everyday scenarios (e.g., picking up a toy and throwing it into a basket) because they lack spatial control over the motion and quantitative feedback on its execution, and they often fail to complete the interaction sequence. To address these gaps, we present Inhabitant, a training-free agent framework in which the agent specifies each motion through positions, paths and poses, measures how the executed interaction deviates from its intent, and revises the control specification accordingly. articles.title: Mapping the Wind to Find the Source: Online Physics-Informed Gas Source Localization with Mobile Robots
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25067v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gas Source Localization (GSL) with mobile robots is challenging because wind and gas measurements are spatially sparse, noisy, and potentially affected by robot motion. Indoor airflow can vary substantially across space, while detailed environmental layouts, boundary conditions, or precomputed airflow fields are often unavailable. Moreover, hazardous sources must be localized as quickly as possible, making exhaustive exploration impractical. This paper presents a lightweight physics-informed probabilistic framework for efficient GSL under spatially varying indoor airflow. As the robot navigates, it continuously collects wind and gas measurements and reconstructs the spatially varying airflow field online. The estimated wind field drives a forward dispersion model that predicts the gas pattern for each candidate source location. articles.title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25105v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample. Built from a pretrained single-robot world-action backbone, MAWAM jointly denoises all robots' action and future-view tokens through cross-agent attention, while preserving a separate control interface for each robot. MAWAM achieves the highest success on all three real-robot tasks (laundry-bag collection, bath-towel folding, and umbrella handover), with 67.8% mean success, 18.9 percentage points above MA-VLA trained on the same demonstrations and cameras. In simulation, MAWAM reaches 90.3% mean success on eight tasks with teams of up to four arms. Ablations show that cross-agent atten

Abstract: Visual world models enable effective short-horizon goal-conditioned planning, such as reaching nearby targets and pushing objects over short distances, by predicting candidate action outcomes and comparing their representations with a goal representation. However, extending this approach to long-horizon tasks is challenging: prediction errors accumulate over extended rollouts, while latent-space similarity to distant goals provides limited guidance for ranking candidate outcomes. Existing methods address these limitations by introducing intermediate subgoals, either generated by learned models or selected from experience memory. articles.title: Old-School Planners Drive (Sometimes) Better Than Learned Ones
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25138v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: End-to-end driving models learn to plan from data, and hand-written planners are widely treated as a thing of the past. We test whether this is justified: we implement sixteen textbook planners, each combining a path source (reference line, A*, hybrid A*, RRT*) with a trajectory method (Frenet lattice, nonlinear optimization, $s$--$t$ search, dynamic window), and evaluate them on three benchmarks: open loop on nuScenes, closed loop on nuPlan with ground-truth perception, and photorealistic closed loop on HUGSIM. On HUGSIM, they replace only the planner of the end-to-end model UniAD and read its frozen perception, without an HD map or other privileged information. On nuScenes and nuPlan, the best textbook planners are competitive (L2 error of 0.735\,m against 0.947\,m for UniAD's planner; a nuPlan score of 79.3 against 76.1 for the rule-based PDM-Closed on Test14-hard with reactive agents). articles.title: From Self-Play RL to Constrained Control: Distilling DiffMPC Students with DAgger
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25197v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Self-play reinforcement learning (RL) produces strong driving policies, but these policies are hard to verify or interpret. Differentiable model predictive control (DiffMPC) can enforce explicit constraints, but it is usually trained by imitating logged data or with costly RL. To add constraints to an already trained policy, we keep a PPO teacher's backbone and replace its action head with a DiffMPC that enforces road boundary half-planes and agent ellipses. We then distill the student with DAgger in the teacher's self-play simulator. Over 9 seeds, the constrained student of a smaller teacher matches its teacher on nuPlan and beats it on CARLA and on out-of-distribution Waymo scenes. For a stronger teacher, the student has fewer failures on nuPlan and Waymo, while staying level on CARLA. Its distillation takes no more than 30% of the teacher's training time.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25199v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adapting robot policies to out-of-distribution (OOD) settings with limited real-world data remains a key bottleneck to generalist robots. The multimodality and scarcity of robotics data lead end-to-end approaches to overfit and break under small distribution shifts. Abstract: Autonomous navigation in diverse real-world environments remains one of the greatest challenges in robotics. It demands both robust low-level motion control to handle diverse terrain and high-level reasoning to interpret environmental cues. We present ROAM (Robust Open-world Autonomous Mobility), a system that enables legged robots to perform kilometer-scale navigation in complex alpine and urban settings. ROAM combines the world knowledge of a Vision-Language Model (VLM), pre-trained on internet-scale data, with robust locomotion and local planning policies learned in simulation via reinforcement learning (RL). Abstract: Ferrofluids are liquids containing magnetic nanoparticles, enabling shape control through external magnetic fields. This deformability supports their use as soft robotic bodies that can navigate confined spaces and manipulate objects. Their nonlinear continuum dynamics, however, make reliable control challenging. articles.content:

Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can propose multi-step manipulation plans, but they have no grounded model of how a scene will change, and the pixel-level world models that could check those plans are slow and drift over long horizons. We present Verify2Act, a modular verification framework that separates semantic action proposal from latent physical verification. A VLM proposes candidate plans, a latent world model (V2A-WM) imagines each of them in the DINOv2 feature space, and a dual-head critic checks the imagined rollouts for temporal consistency and goal satisfaction before anything is executed. V2A-WM extends recent flow-matching world models with cross-attention action grounding and a causal temporal history window. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25249v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic cyber-physical systems rely on perception and state estimation to support autonomous decisions. Degraded, inconsistent, or manipulated sensor observations can therefore propagate through an autonomous pipeline and create security-relevant failures. This work presents a synthetic Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (C-UAS) testbed developed in NVIDIA Isaac Sim for repeatable stress testing of perception and tracking algorithms supporting agentic decision-making. A simplified quadrotor follows scripted trajectories while co-located virtual sensors generate synchronized RGB, RTX LiDAR, and illustrative IR-like observations. The testbed varies target range, motion, clutter, occlusion, and sensor availability, with future stress cases including sensor dropout, temporal misalignment, cross-modal disagreement, and false observations. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25254v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous robots may need to adapt both their task plans and architectural configurations as operating conditions change. These decisions are interdependent: architectural configurations determine which actions a robot can perform, while task plans determine which capabilities are required. This paper presents PLANTA, an ontology-mediated approach to task and architecture co-adaptation that considers these dependencies during mission planning. PLANTA uses an ontology expressed in the Web Ontology Language to represent architectural alternatives and their associated functional and quality requirements, while the Planning Domain Definition Language defines task actions and mission goals. By automatically translating and integrating these models, PLANTA enables joint planning of task and reconfiguration actions. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25202v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Crisis and disaster governance increasingly relies on technologies that sense, classify and act faster than humans can. Drone swarms coordinated with human operators, known as human-swarm teaming, provide a productive case to review the field of crisis governance. They promise better situational awareness in disaster response, but they also raise questions about human control, responsibility, surveillance, triage, dual use and public legitimacy. This report maps the ethical and societal territory that HST opens up. It unpacks this territory with a 3i-framework, the Interface, where operators and swarms work together, the Infrastructure, where organisations distribute tasks, decisions and blame, and the Imaginary, where law, policy and shared societal assumptions define what a crisis is and which interventions it justifies. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25320v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Residual reinforcement learning corrects an imitation-trained base policy using a limited budget of environment interaction. In a task with several phases, this budget must be divided among the phases, and the phase in which the base policy fails is not necessarily the phase in which a correction most improves task completion. We formalize this distinction through the completion gain: the change in full-task completion probability when, during a single phase, a state-feedback controller replaces selected components of the base policy's action. We decompose the completion gain into the probability of reaching the phase and the conditional improvement in completion from the start of the phase, and we estimate it from paired episodes. articles.title: FlowDrive: moderated flow matching with data balancing for trajectory planning
articles.content:
arXiv:2509.21961v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Learning-based planners are sensitive to the long-tailed distribution of driving data. Common maneuvers dominate datasets, while dangerous or rare scenarios are sparse. This imbalance can bias models toward the frequent cases and degrade performance on critical scenarios. To tackle this problem, we compare balancing strategies for sampling training data and find reweighting by trajectory pattern an effective approach. We then present FlowDrive, a flow-matching trajectory planner that learns a conditional rectified flow to map noise directly to trajectory distributions with few flow-matching steps. We further introduce moderated, in-the-loop guidance that injects small perturbation between flow steps to systematically increase trajectory diversity while remaining scene-consistent. articles.content:
arXiv:2602.07629v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We propose LCLA (Language-Conditioned Latent Alignment), a framework for vision-language navigation that learns modular perception-action interfaces by aligning sensory observations to a latent representation of an expert policy. The expert is first trained with privileged state information, inducing a latent space sufficient for control, after which its latent interface and action head are frozen. A lightweight adapter is then trained to map raw visual-language observations, via a frozen vision-language model, into the expert's latent space, reducing the problem of visuomotor learning to supervised latent alignment rather than end-to-end policy optimization. This decoupling enforces a stable contract between perception and control, enabling expert behavior to be reused across sensing modalities and environmental variations. articles.content:
arXiv:2602.18224v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models often bundle architectural changes with different pretraining data, backbone scales, and optimization recipes, obscuring what actually drives progress. We introduce SimVLA, a deliberately minimal VLA, a standard vision-language backbone with a lightweight continuous-action head, as a controlled testbed for this attribution problem; our contribution is methodological and empirical (a controlled attribution study and a minimal-baseline calibration), not a new technique. articles.content: Scaling Law在空间智能这里失效了？    作者丨周蕾    编辑丨岑峰                                                                                                       今年初字节的Seedance 2.0发布时，“电影级别”的出片质量让不少从业者倍感兴奋和震撼，新的创作蓝图正在他们面前徐徐展开——但对商汤的Seko团队来说，那是一段“迷茫”的日子。商汤联合创始人、首席科学家林达华在最近一次访谈中回忆，那段时间他去见投资人、参加行业会议，被问到的几乎总是同一个问题：你们的Seko和Seedance有什么区别？做得过它吗？团队里一度出现自我怀疑的声音：这件事还要不要做下去？后来故事并没有走向商汤Seko单枪匹马“对抗”Seedance的结局。Seedance把30秒的视频片段渲染到顶级水准；而Seko面向的创作者，最终交付的是100集的短剧——这中间隔着剧本、分镜、人物设定和跨剧集的形象一致性，是一整套创作流程。想清楚了这件事，Seko反而活得更好了：据林达华在访谈中透露，今年这款产品的用户增长了7到8倍，平台上产出了播放量过亿的短剧。对于商汤在大模型市场上的声量，林达华自己有个坦率的评价：“可能不是最大的”。这家公司的路线，也始终没有完全跟着行业最热的方向走。但商汤有一个坚持多年的习惯：直到今天，公司依然有20%的资源，投入给没有任何产品出口的预研工作。某种程度来说，这也是一种“播种”，种子下地时其实无需承诺收成。汤晓鸥常挂在嘴边的那句话——life finds a way，“生命自寻出路”，或许正是这笔投入的逻辑。在最近参加的微博科技 X 卫诗婕联合出品的《科技漫谈》栏目访谈中，林达华从行业的现状聊起，穿过商业化的验证，最后落在智能的边界上。但贯穿始终的线索只有一个：那20%的资源，以及支撑它的判断——为什么有的路值得走得很长、很久，哪怕眼下仍未看见出口。01训练成本停不下来，拼手速的中国AI大模型行业的钱，正在以一种停不下来的方式烧下去。行业里曾经有一个普遍假设：花巨大代价训出一个好模型，成本就能摊薄到之后的规模化服务里。林达华在访谈中指出，这个假设未必成立——问题不在模型不够好，而是“你不继续训下一个，别人就会超过你”。竞争逼着公司一轮接一轮地重训，训练成本因此停不下来，而且越滚越大。尽管过去一年的行业叙事，几乎被“更大即更强”占据，但卷参数这条路正在遭到反噬。他提到两个信号：一是模型的体量选择变得更务实。最近各家厂商均发布了Flash级别的中小模型：GLM 5.3 Flash、DeepSeek 4.1 Flash，谷歌和OpenAI也推出了同类规格的产品。林达华在访谈中特别提到了DeepSeek的表现：“4.1的Flash，它的性能水平是比4.0 Pro是要好的。”一个几百B量级、训练调优精良的模型跑赢上一代Pro，说明中等体量上的优化空间还远没有吃完。二是预训练数据的质量被重新摆上桌面。当几千亿参数的模型在实战中跑赢了2万亿参数的对手，很多人开始回头检查自己的数据管线。林达华对此有一个形象的解释：“（数据里）有很多的杂质、很多的东西相互打架，使得中间的很多的效率就会被抵扣掉。”结果就是一个又贵又不理想的模型，参数堆上去了，效果没上去。“当所有人很盲目地去做参数量的竞争，我觉得并不是一种健康的状态。”在他看来，这两个信号意味着行业正在回归理性：不再围着单一指标较劲，而是回到最终用户的价值上。上一轮AI周期里，类似情况也出现过，商汤自己就是亲历者。每个项目都要从收集数据开始，专门训练、调优、测试，全流程重做一遍，很难真正复制。只是当年的计量单位是项目，今天换成了参数。拼手速是另一种内卷的形态。美国的前沿实验室定义着SOTA的天花板，新模型一发布，等于给中国的从业者们指了一条路——国内往往在两三个月内涌出一批宣称采用同类方案的产品，抢占生态位，最近大热的RSI（递归自我改进）同样是一堆公司在同时开建。“说实话，拼手速这个事其实是蛮累的。”林达华观察

articles.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
articles.content: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.

articles.title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
articles.content: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. On SD3.5-M, these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints, with no reward in the objective. Although the vectors are identical for every prompt, token, and sampling seed, they recover 90.0-96.3% of the reward gains of six RL-tuned image models, and 89.8% and 111.9% on two RL-tuned video models. Initialized at zero and trained with online RL, the vectors alone exceed the reward gains of weight-based RL on text rendering (OCR) and human preference (PickScore) on SD3.5-M. A constant shift thus suffices for most of the gain of policy-gradient RL post-training: without new input-dependent transformations, it steers the pretrained generator toward what it can already compute.

articles.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
articles.content: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game. It estimates player abilities, predicts performance at different proficiency levels, and compares those predictions with a target learning progression. It diagnoses the game and addresses the gaps by giving players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution. We evaluate games in fresh runs with player agents across three intelligence settings, measuring learning gain and learning slope. Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games. It also outperforms the baselines on the macro-average of each metric at every intelligence setting.
